audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart hands Ryze all seven stages, but every why beneath it says the opposite for the early game: whys[0] 'you absorb his poke for free', whys[1] 'a short burst trade where you knock him up and walk out is possible', whys[3] 'your Permafrost stun chain outpaces his mana-expensive rotation at levels 4-5 and farm advantage is yours'. The file also stores 53.44% for Sejuani, and the packet's own chart reads Sejuani, Sejuani, Skill, Sejuani, Ryze, Skill, Skill.
audit.why: A 7/7 enemy chart on a matchup Sejuani wins, contradicted by its own explanations.
audit.corrected: Levels 1, 2 and 4-5 should read Sejuani, level 3 and first item Skill. Not written as edits: a side value cannot change inside the +/-10% length band, so the applier or mirror-fix has to set it. Raised in questionsForUser.

audit.why: Spikes at Sejuani 1-2, Sejuani 3, Ryze 6 and Ryze two items are the right shape — she front-loads, he scales — and the level-6 spike is genuinely his because Rune Prison answers her landing.

audit.whatIsWrong: 1) mid says to 'respect that he has a passive shield on his W cast' and spikes[2] credits him 'his shield'. Ryze has no shield in his kit; his passive is Arcane Mastery, which adds damage from bonus mana and max mana from AP. 2) Rune Prison is treated as an unconditional root everywhere. Riot's text: it damages and slows, and only roots if the target already has Flux on them. The tell is therefore Spell Flux (E) landing first, not the W cast. 3) Because Fury of the North's Frost Armor grants immunity to slows, an un-Fluxed Rune Prison does nothing to a Sejuani who has been out of combat. 4) The combo is written 'W-EQ' and 'his EQ combo'; the real order is E to apply Flux, then W to root, then the amplified Q.
audit.why: A fabricated shield sets the trading rule, and the single condition that decides whether his lockdown exists at all is missing.
audit.corrected: Shield removed, Rune Prison's Flux condition stated with Spell Flux as the tell, Frost Armor's slow immunity used, and the combo order corrected to E into W into Q.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says 'he has no lockdown for the next 13 seconds' after Rune Prison.
audit.why: Rune Prison is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9 — 11 seconds at rank 1, not 13. Spell Flux is 3.5s, which is why the Flux tell matters more than the W timer.
audit.corrected: 11 seconds used, and Spell Flux's 3.5s named as the thing that actually cycles.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sejuani's resistances are called 'passive Permafrost resistances' in spikes[0] and wants.you[0].
audit.why: Permafrost is the E stun; the resistances and the slow immunity are Fury of the North's Frost Armor, and whys[0] already names it correctly, so the page contradicts itself.

edits.before: Level 3 is your window: Q knockup into double W (both strikes land a Frost stack) into Permafrost stun is your full chain, and it hurts a squishy mage who spent his Rune Prison cooldown randomly rooting minions. Bait the W root by stepping forward — let it fire, sidestep or eat it, then immediately Q in because he has no lockdown for the next 13 seconds. At levels 4-5 respect that he has a passive shield on his W cast; trade just after he uses it defensively. Your level 6 Glacial Prison looks good on paper but Ryze can instantly root you with W when you land nearby, interrupting your follow-up — use the comet from max range to stun him across the wave rather than close-range where he roots you into his full rotation.
edits.after: Level 3 is your window: Q knockup into double W (both strikes land a Frost stack) into Permafrost stun is your full chain, and it hurts a squishy mage who spent Rune Prison randomly slowing minions. Watch Spell Flux, not the W cast — Rune Prison only roots a target that already has Flux on it, and against Frost Armor an un-Fluxed one does not even slow you. Bait the Flux, then Q in, because Rune Prison is 11 seconds at rank 1. At levels 4-5 trade just after he burns it. Your level 6 Glacial Prison looks good on paper but Ryze can root you the moment you land beside him, so throw the comet from max range across the wave rather than closing into his rotation.

edits.before: Glacial Prison lets Ryze throw Rune Prison and land his EQ combo, which combined with his shield gives him a reliable counter-engage and turns your all-in into a coinflip.
edits.after: Glacial Prison lets Ryze answer with Spell Flux into Rune Prison and the amplified Overload behind it, which gives him a reliable counter-engage and turns your all-in into a coinflip.

edits.before: Glacial Prison gives Ryze a predictable landing point; he roots you with W and lands EQ before your team can follow — his lockdown on your lockdown flips the level 6 spike.
edits.after: Glacial Prison gives Ryze a predictable landing point; he Fluxes you, roots with Rune Prison and lands Overload before your team can follow — his lockdown on your lockdown flips level 6.

edits.before: Root you with W when you step forward, then land the instant EQ combo while you cannot move or use Arctic Assault to escape
edits.after: Land Spell Flux first so Rune Prison roots instead of slowing, then land the amplified Overload while you cannot move

edits.before: Your passive Permafrost resistances are fully stacked before the first poke lands — Ryze's Q spam cannot chunk through Fury of the North this early, giving you free CS.
edits.after: Fury of the North's Frost Armor is fully stacked before the first poke lands — Ryze's Q spam cannot chunk through it this early, and it ignores Rune Prison's slow, giving you free CS.

edits.before: Absorb his Q poke behind minions and stack Permafrost resistances passively so he can never get you low enough to force you off CS
edits.after: Absorb his Q poke behind minions and let Fury of the North's Frost Armor rebuild, so he can never get you low enough to force you off CS

edits.before: Both W strikes apply Frost at level 3, meaning one Q-in gives you the Permafrost stun immediately — but he has the same stun chain threat with W-EQ, so the window is genuinely contested.
edits.after: Both W strikes apply Frost at level 3, meaning one Q-in gives you the Permafrost stun immediately — but his Spell Flux into Rune Prison into Overload answers it, so the window is genuinely contested.

edits.before: Hit the Q knockup into double-W into Permafrost stun chain when Rune Prison is down — that is your only burst window before he roots you
edits.after: Hit the Q knockup into double-W into Permafrost chain while Rune Prison's 11 seconds run — that is your burst window before he roots you

edits.before: - Ryze Rune Prison (Root): matchup-defining — Point-blank root — respect the EQ chain that follows it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your Q dash has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Ryze Rune Prison: 11s at rank 1, and it only roots if Spell Flux (3.5s) landed on you first — otherwise it is a slow Frost Armor ignores. - Watch the Flux, not the cage. - Your Q dash is the exit; the R is the opening.

notes: Two fabricated mechanics removed: a 'passive shield on his W cast' (Ryze has no shield; his passive is Arcane Mastery, bonus damage from bonus mana and bonus max mana from AP) and Rune Prison as an unconditional root. Riot's text is explicit that Rune Prison damages and slows, and only roots a target that already has Flux on it — so Spell Flux (3.5s) is the real tell, and against Fury of the North's Frost Armor an un-Fluxed Rune Prison is a slow she is immune to. Cooldown corrected from 'the next 13 seconds' to 11 at rank 1, and the combo order from 'W-EQ' to E into W into Q.
